stages.text: This is what really happens underneath when Emma asks Ask Northbridge for something. We will follow one real request, recorded in our sandbox, from her chat window into the Ledgerline ERP and back. Every number you see on screen comes from that run.
stages.say: This is what really happens underneath when Emma asks Ask Northbridge for something. We will follow one real request, recorded in our sandbox, from her chat window into the Ledgerline ERP and back. Every number you see on screen comes from that run.

stages.text: Emma types one sentence: how many city e-bike battery packs do we have? Her message goes to the harness. The harness is plain code that sits around the model and runs the conversation.
stages.say: Emma types one sentence: how many city e-bike battery packs do we have? Her message goes to the harness. The harness is plain code that sits around the model and runs the conversation.

stages.text: Before the model sees anything, the harness builds one request. The system prompt with our rules, 196 tokens. Emma's message, 11 tokens. And the descriptions of all 15 tools, 1,932 tokens. A token is a small piece of text, about three quarters of a word, so the model receives 2,139 tokens.
stages.say: Before the model sees anything, the harness builds one request. The system prompt with our rules, 196 tokens. Emma's message, 11 tokens. And the descriptions of all 15 tools, 1,932 tokens. A token is a small piece of text, about three quarters of a word, so the model receives 2,139 tokens.

stages.text: The model reads those 2,139 tokens and makes a decision. It does not answer yet. It picks one tool out of fifteen, find_item, and writes its arguments as a small piece of JSON: the query, city e-bike battery pack. That is 21 tokens out, in under three seconds.
stages.say: The model reads those 2,139 tokens and makes a decision. It does not answer yet. It picks one tool out of fifteen, find item, and writes its arguments as a small piece of JSON: the query, city e-bike battery pack. That is 21 tokens out, in under three seconds.

stages.text: The harness does not trust that call blindly. The guard checks it against the tool's own schema: is this a real tool, and are the arguments the right type? It passes, so the call travels over MCP, the standard plug between the model's side and our tools.
stages.say: The harness does not trust that call blindly. The guard checks it against the tool's own schema: is this a real tool, and are the arguments the right type? It passes, so the call travels over M C P, the standard plug between the model's side and our tools.

stages.text: Now the tool runs, with Emma's own permissions. It calls the Ledgerline services eleven times, searching for items and reading them. For us Ledgerline is a black box: data goes in, data comes out.
stages.say: Now the tool runs, with Emma's own permissions. It calls the Ledgerline services eleven times, searching for items and reading them. For us Ledgerline is a black box: data goes in, data comes out.

stages.text: The result comes back as JSON, and the harness adds it to the conversation. Then it calls the model again. The next request is already 2,507 tokens, because every step makes the context a little longer.
stages.say: The result comes back as JSON, and the harness adds it to the conversation. Then it calls the model again. The next request is already 2,507 tokens, because every step makes the context a little longer.

stages.text: The model wants to be sure which item is the city e-bike pack, so it calls search_policy. This tool reads our manuals and policy documents, not the ERP.
stages.say: The model wants to be sure which item is the city e-bike pack, so it calls search policy. This tool reads our manuals and policy documents, not the E R P.

stages.text: Now it calls check_stock for BAT-500. Ledgerline says 5,400 packs in Manchester and 1,200 in Leeds: 6,600 in all, about 11 days of cover.
stages.say: Now it calls check stock for BAT 500. Ledgerline says 5,400 packs in Manchester and 1,200 in Leeds: 6,600 in all, about 11 days of cover.

stages.text: It also checks the refurbished pack, BAT-500-R, and this time the tool says no: ok is false, with an error and a next step. A tool failing cleanly like this is normal. The model reads it like any other result.
stages.say: It also checks the refurbished pack, BAT 500 R, and this time the tool says no. O K is false, with an error and a next step. A tool failing cleanly like this is normal. The model reads it like any other result.

stages.text: Now the model has what it needs, so it calls no tool. It writes the answer from the tool results: 6,600 packs, 11 days of cover. Five model calls and four tool calls, for one simple question.
stages.say: Now the model has what it needs, so it calls no tool. It writes the answer from the tool results: 6,600 packs, 11 days of cover. Five model calls and four tool calls, for one simple question.

stages.text: Next, Emma asks for real work: order 2,000 battery packs from Voltway Cells for the spring launch run, cost centre PRD-07, needed by 9 November.
stages.say: Next, Emma asks for real work: order 2,000 battery packs from Voltway Cells for the spring launch run, cost centre P R D zero seven, needed by the ninth of November.

stages.text: The model starts with the supplier. find_supplier returns Voltway Cells in Eindhoven, with the supplier code it needs.
stages.say: The model starts with the supplier. Find supplier returns Voltway Cells in Eindhoven, with the supplier code it needs.

stages.text: Then it checks the rules for direct orders in our policy documents.
stages.say: Then it checks the rules for direct orders in our policy documents.

stages.text: It tries to create a purchase order directly, and Ledgerline's rule says no. A direct order is limited to £50,000, and this one is £285,600. The next step comes back with it: raise a purchase request first.
stages.say: It tries to create a purchase order directly, and Ledgerline's rule says no. A direct order is limited to fifty thousand pounds, and this one is two hundred and eighty-five thousand, six hundred pounds. The next step comes back with it: raise a purchase request first.

stages.text: So it checks the budget on PRD-07, the spring launch run. The cost centre is open.
stages.say: So it checks the budget on P R D zero seven, the spring launch run. The cost centre is open.

stages.text: Now it calls create_purchase_request with confirm set to false. That means preview only: nothing is saved. The preview says £273,600, and Daniel Okafor must approve it.
stages.say: Now it calls create purchase request, with confirm set to false. That means preview only: nothing is saved. The preview says two hundred and seventy-three thousand, six hundred pounds, and Daniel Okafor must approve it.

stages.text: The model shows Emma that preview and asks her to confirm. Nothing changes in the ERP until she says yes.
stages.say: The model shows Emma that preview and asks her to confirm. Nothing changes in the E R P until she says yes.

stages.text: Emma says: yes, go ahead.
stages.say: Emma says: yes, go ahead.

stages.text: Now the same tool runs with confirm set to true. Ledgerline saves the request and submits it, and because it is above Emma's limit, it lands in Daniel's approval inbox as PR/2026/04417.
stages.say: Now the same tool runs, with confirm set to true. Ledgerline saves the request and submits it, and because it is above Emma's limit, it lands in Daniel's approval inbox, as purchase request zero four four one seven.

stages.text: Finally, the tool reads the request back from Ledgerline. That receipt, not the model's own words, is what Emma sees: PR/2026/04417, waiting for approval from Daniel. That is the whole loop: the harness builds the context, the model picks a tool, the guard checks it, MCP carries it, and the ERP does the work.
